title: Quick request: short privacy bullets for procurement (DPA + subprocessors)
text:
Quick request: short privacy bullets for procurement (DPA + subprocessors)

['From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acme-corp.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Quick: privacy bullets for procurement (DPA/subprocessors)

Hi Mateo,

Procurement at Acme is asking for a very short set of bullets we can hand to legal — they want to know how Redwood handles the DPA, subprocessors, and international transfers for the hosted API/console.

Can you send a 3-5 bullet summary (plain language) and any one-pager you have? They want something I can attach to the SOW review later today.

Thanks — Jordan

Jordan Miles
Sr. Platform PM, Acme Corp
jordan.miles@acme-corp.com
', 'From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Quick: privacy bullets for procurement (DPA/subprocessors)

Laura / Lauren — forwarding Jordan's note from Acme (below). They need a very short, public-friendly bulleted summary and an attachable one-pager for procurement/legal.

Constraints:
- Keep it vendor-facing (sales-friendly), but legally safe — avoid new commitments beyond the DPA.
- Highlight hosted API specifics (data-in-transit/residency options, subprocessors list availability, transfers safeguards).
- One-paragraph 1–2 line "tooltip" for console UI would be great too.

Can you draft 3–5 bullets + a 2-line console blurb? Kim, looping you for quick legal sanity check on phrasing and to point to the latest dpa doc. Jordan wants this today if possible.

Thanks — Mateo
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
', 'From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick: privacy bullets for procurement (DPA/subprocessors)

Mateo — draft below. I attached two stubs: redwood_dpa_onepager_v1.pdf (one-pager tailored for procurement) and subprocessor_map_snapshot_202609.csv (exports current subprocessors list). I kept language conservative and referential so we don't create new contractual obligations.

Suggested bullets (3–5):
1) DPA & commitments: Redwood provides a standard DPA that includes processor obligations, security controls, and data subject support. Customers may sign our DPA or incorporate it by reference into their agreement.

2) Subprocessors: We maintain a current subprocessor map; customers can request notifications and a list at any time. Subprocessor use is covered by our DPA and contractual flow-downs.

3) International transfers & safeguards: For cross-border transfers we rely on appropriate safeguards (standard contractual clauses and equivalent mechanisms) and technical protections such as encryption in transit and at rest.

4) Hosted API specifics: Data sent to the hosted API is processed in customer-selected regions where available; telemetry and logs are retained per agreed retention settings. For regulated workloads, Dedicated or Private deployments can be used to meet stricter residency or isolation needs.

5) Security & controls: We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), audit logging, and SOC 2 controls; more detail is available in the DPA and security documentation.

Console tooltip (1–2 lines):
"Redwood processes requests under our DPA; subprocessors are listed and updated regularly. Choose a data residency option or contact sales for Dedicated/Private deployment if you require isolation"

Notes for Kim: we avoided naming transfer mechanisms in the tooltip — left that to the DPA/one-pager. If legal is okay with this language, Mateo, I recommend sending Jordan the attached one-pager and the CSV snapshot.

Attachments: 1) redwood_dpa_onepager_v1.pdf (one-pager summary) 2) subprocessor_map_snapshot_202609.csv (current snapshot)

Laura Bennett
Head of Trust & Compliance (Content)
Redwood Inference
', "From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick: privacy bullets for procurement (DPA/subprocessors)

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the nudge. Please find a very short summary below (feel free to include it with your procurement packet) and I attached our one-pager + current subprocessor snapshot. If you want, we can hop on a 15-minute call to run through any questions Acme's legal team might have.

Short bullets for procurement (copy/paste):
• DPA & commitments: Redwood provides a standard Data Processing Addendum that defines processor responsibilities and security protections; you can sign our DPA or incorporate by reference.
• Subprocessors: A current subprocessor map is available on request; subprocessors are contractually bound to our DPA obligations.
• Transfers & safeguards: Cross-border transfers use appropriate legal safeguards (SCCs or equivalent) and technical protections (encryption in transit + at rest).
• Hosted API options: Hosted processing can be regionally restricted where available; Dedicated/Private deployments offer additional data isolation for regulated workloads.

Attachments included: redwood_dpa_onepager_v1.pdf, subprocessor_map_snapshot_202609.csv

Would you like me to send the formal DPA or loop legal for a short review call?

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
"]
